chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, all from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries a woman and does not assign a dower (mahr) for her, so he dies from her or divorces her before he has entered (consummated) with her. What is for her against him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dower for her, and she inherits him, and he inherits her.'

key_terms.صَدَاقاً: Dower or bride price assigned to the wife
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: To enter with her, meaning consummation of marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dower and inheritance if a husband dies or divorces his wife before consummation without assigning a specific mahr?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific legal status of a 'non-consummated' marriage (nikah ghayr daakhil) where no dower was explicitly stipulated, ruling that the wife inherits from her husband and vice versa despite the absence of mahr. This ruling is derived from the principle that the marriage contract itself establishes the mutual inheritance right, distinguishing it from cases where consummation triggers the obligation of full dower. It highlights the Shia juristic view that inheritance is a consequence of the valid contract rather than solely of sexual union.
